title: Siemens and NVIDIA tout Agentic AI - Semiwiki
gist: At DAC 2026 Siemens and NVIDIA showed self-verifying, long-running agents driving GPU-accelerated EDA tools, built on Siemens' Fuse EDA and Intelligence Center X with NVIDIA's Nemotron models, NeMo Gym, CUDA-X libraries and MCP architecture. Daniel Payne's read is that the industry moved in one year from AI inside EDA tools to agents controlling EDA tools, with design times compressing from days to hours while deterministic physics-based engines remain the authority.

insights.claim: The EDA industry moved in a single year from embedding AI inside individual tools to deploying agents that control the EDA tools themselves, a pace of change described as brisk by an attendee comparing DAC 2025 with DAC 2026.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Agentic orchestration is the new competitive axis in EDA; vendors still selling point-tool AI features are already a generation behind.
insights.quote: DAC 2025 was all about using AI within EDA tools, and this year I see Agents controlling EDA tools, so the progress in just one year has been brisk.

insights.claim: The newest capability shown at DAC 2026 is self-verifying and long-running agents driving GPU-accelerated EDA tools with a human in the loop, an advance over the plan-orchestrate-execute agent demonstrated at NVIDIA GTC in March.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Self-verification is the unlock that lets agents run unattended for long stretches — the gating capability for real labor leverage in design.
insights.quote: At DAC the news is that there are now self-verifying and long-running agents that are using GPU-accelerated EDA tools, with human in the loop.
insights.locator: Last year Siemens launched Fuse EDA

insights.claim: Agentic AI applied to semiconductor and PCB flows is compressing design times from days to hours, according to a DAC 2026 attendee reporting on the Siemens-NVIDIA collaboration.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: An order-of-magnitude cycle-time claim; if it holds, design-services and verification headcount economics change materially.
insights.quote: Compressing design times from days to hours is happening with agentic AI like this.

insights.claim: The domains that agentic AI addresses in chip and board design are expected to expand over time rather than remain confined to today's use cases.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Implies a widening TAM for agentic EDA subscriptions rather than a one-off feature sale.
insights.quote: You can expect the domains that agentic AI address to build over time.

insights.claim: Siemens launched Fuse EDA, an AI system for agentic semiconductor and PCB design, and has now integrated it into its new Intelligence Center X product.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Names the specific Siemens product line carrying its agentic strategy — the SKU to track for EDA AI monetization.
insights.locator: Last year Siemens launched Fuse EDA

insights.claim: Siemens has already embedded AI across a broad EDA portfolio spanning Catapult for high-level synthesis, Calibre for physical verification, Solido for IC library characterization, Tessent for DFT, Questa One and Veloce for verification, and Aprisa for physical implementation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: The breadth means Siemens can orchestrate agents across an end-to-end flow, a structural advantage over single-point AI EDA startups.
insights.locator: Siemens has used AI technology within several EDA tools

insights.claim: Siemens' AI infrastructure extends beyond chip tools into Teamcenter, Simcenter, Designcenter and Digital Twin Composer, letting the same agent approach reach design, manufacturing and supply chain operations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Siemens is positioning agentic AI as an industrial-software play, not an EDA-only one — a wider revenue surface than pure-play EDA rivals.
insights.locator: In Siemens design and engineering tools

insights.claim: Siemens frames its AI-native tools as combining faster engines and smarter execution while still providing deterministic results, keeping reproducibility as an explicit product requirement.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Determinism is the credibility currency in EDA; any agentic pitch lacking it will fail customer qualification regardless of speed claims.
insights.quote: At Siemens they are bringing out AI-native tools and flows with faster engines, and smarter execution, all while providing deterministic results.
insights.locator: Industry trends are that AI accelerators

insights.claim: NVIDIA supplies the agentic substrate under Siemens' EDA flows through Nemotron open models for token efficiency, NeMo Gym to make agents run smarter, and OpenShell for secure operations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is monetizing AI software layers, not only silicon — evidence its moat is widening upward into agent tooling.
insights.quote: NVIDIA NeMo Gym makes the agents run smarter, Nemotron models are used for token efficiency, all running under the OpenShell for secure operations.
insights.locator: Last year Siemens launched Fuse EDA

insights.claim: Siemens' Intelligence Center X is built on NVIDIA's CUDA-X libraries for both agent creation and orchestration, tying a major EDA vendor's agent platform directly to NVIDIA's software stack.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: CUDA-X dependency at the orchestration layer deepens NVIDIA lock-in in EDA and raises the switching cost of any AMD or alternative-accelerator migration.
insights.locator: Siemens’ Intelligence Center X uses the CUDA-X libraries

insights.claim: The Fuse EDA AI Agent uses the Model Context Protocol architecture to plan, orchestrate and execute workflows across semiconductor and PCB design, making MCP a de facto integration standard inside commercial EDA.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: MCP adoption by an EDA major raises the odds it becomes the industry's tool-integration standard, favoring vendors already shipping MCP servers.
insights.locator: This year in March at the NVIDIA GTC event

insights.claim: NVIDIA has built CUDA-X libraries across genomics, medical imaging, quantum computing, physics, deep learning, CAE and numerical computing, so EDA is one more vertical extension of an existing accelerated-library playbook rather than a new capability.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: The vertical-library pattern is repeatable, which is why NVIDIA's software attach keeps compounding across unrelated industries.
insights.locator: Over the years NVIDIA has provided CUDA-X libraries

insights.claim: Transistor counts in systems are heading toward the trillions, and conventional design methods are simply too slow to handle that scale, which is the stated technical forcing function for agentic AI in EDA.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Complexity growth, not cost-cutting, is the demand driver — meaning agentic EDA spend is defensive and less discretionary than it looks.
insights.quote: Tim shared how the explosive transistor counts of systems reaching soon into the trillions require new methods like AI, as the old ways are just too slow.
insights.locator: Tim shared how the explosive transistor counts

insights.claim: The four industry trends framing the Siemens-NVIDIA push are AI accelerators being embedded into chips, software-defined products driving hardware implementations, continued growth in multi-die integration, and power efficiency becoming a requirement rather than an option.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A compact checklist of the structural demand drivers behind chiplet, packaging and power-management supply chains.
insights.locator: Industry trends are that AI accelerators

insights.claim: Audience questions at the Siemens-NVIDIA session centered on how agents work, whether AI results can be trusted, and self-verification, indicating trust rather than capability is the live adoption obstacle among EDA practitioners.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Customer trust is the bottleneck to conversion, so vendors that ship verifiable evidence trails will convert pilots to seats faster.
insights.quote: questions were answered about how agents work, trusting AI results, self-verification, EDA flows within NVIDIA, and where agents are used at Siemens
